candidate.answerReason: Every real square is nonnegative, and \(0\in[-1,2]\) gives \(f(0)=0\). Hence the minimum is 0.

methods.label: Locate the vertex in the interval
methods.explanation: The vertex at \(x=0\) lies in the interval \([-1,2]\), and \(f(0)=0\); the endpoint values are 1 and 4. The minimum value is 0.
methods.levelReason: Uses the vertex of the basic upward-opening parabola and the specified interval, without calculus.

methods.label: Use the sign of a square
methods.explanation: Every real square is nonnegative, so \(f(x)=x^2\ge0\). Since \(0\in[-1,2]\) and \(f(0)=0\), this lower bound is attained. The minimum value is \(0\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary square-sign rules and attainment of the bound, requiring less graph knowledge than the main method.
